full_text_en:
Spider King Group Co., Ltd. v. Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and American Spider Group Co., Ltd. — Administrative Dispute over Trademark Opposition Review

【Ruling Summary】

In the administrative procedure for trademark authorization and confirmation, a distinction should be made between the continuation of goodwill and the continuation of a trademark. The goodwill accumulated by a market participant in the course of business operations may be transferred and continued, but the market conduct of such participant is not automatically legitimate in result merely because of its legitimate purpose. Where a market participant, for the purpose of transferring or continuing goodwill, separately registers a new trademark that has a certain connection with the originally registered trademark, it must still be examined by the trademark administration authority in accordance with the law.

Supreme People's Court
Administrative Ruling

(2017) Zui Gao Fa Xing Shen No. 3297

Reapplying Petitioner (Third Party at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): American Spider Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Unit A5, 9/F, Silvermark International Tower, 707-713 Nathan Road, Mongkok, Kowloon, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Wang Yongshan, Executive Director of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Yong, attorney at Beijing Jincheng Tongda & Neal Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Jin Chenlin, intern attorney at Beijing Jincheng Tongda & Neal Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Spider King Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Oujiang Third Bridge Industrial Zone, Yongjia County, Zhejiang Province.
Legal Representative: Xu Chengjian, Chairman of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wu Congmei, attorney at Beijing Wuhuida (Shanghai) Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance: Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce. Domicile: No. 1 Chama South Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Zhao Gang, Director of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Li Mengmeng, Examiner of the Board.

In the administrative dispute over trademark opposition review between the reapplying petitioner American Spider Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as American Spider Company) and the respondent Spider King Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Spider King Group Company), as well as the defendant at first instance and appellant at second instance Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Review Board), American Spider Company, dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2016) Jing Zhong No. 4490 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court, filed a petition with this Court for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the review, which has now been concluded.

American Spider Company petitions for retrial on the following grounds: (1) Trademark No. 4312222 (the opposed trademark in this case, hereinafter referred to as the Opposed Trademark) is a continuation registration by American Spider Company based on its prior registered Trademark No. 1212760 "Zhongji ZHONGJI and design" (hereinafter referred to as Trademark No. 1212760). The constituent elements, overall visual effect, etc., of the Opposed Trademark are identical to the graphic part of Trademark No. 1212760, and the goods designated for use under the Opposed Trademark are the same as those approved for use under Trademark No. 1212760, namely: clothing, baby clothing, swimwear, hats, socks, ties, scarves, belts, shoes, and gloves. Therefore, the Opposed Trademark should be approved for registration. (2) The Opposed Trademark has formed a stable market pattern through American Spider Company's continuous use and promotion. American Spider Company has been continuously using Trademark No. 1212760, already occupying a certain market share and forming a stable market pattern. Moreover, Trademark No. 1212760 has coexisted in the market for many years with Trademark No. 1027408 "Spider King ZHIZHUWANG and design" (the first cited trademark in this case, hereinafter referred to as Citation Trademark I), Trademark No. 1637185 (a purely graphical trademark, the second cited trademark in this case, hereinafter referred to as Citation Trademark II), and Trademark No. 2005562 (a purely graphical trademark, the third cited trademark in this case, hereinafter referred to as Citation Trademark III), without causing confusion among consumers. (3) The Opposed Trademark does not constitute a similar trademark to Citation Trademarks I, II, and III used on the same or similar goods. The Opposed Trademark and Citation Trademark I differ significantly in terms of textual composition, constituent elements, and overall visual effect, and thus do not constitute similar trademarks. The Opposed Trademark and Citation Trademarks II and III have certain differences in terms of compositional details and overall visual effect, and even if they coexist in the market, they would not cause confusion or misidentification among relevant consumers. (4) The Opposed Trademark is a continuation registration by American Spider Company of its prior registered Trademark No. 1212760 and should be approved for registration. On this point, the court of first instance failed to provide commentary, constituting an omission in trial; the court of second instance erred in its finding that "the coexistence of Trademark No. 1212760 with Citation Trademarks II and III cannot serve as a basis for whether the Opposed Trademark should be approved for registration."

In summary, American Spider Company petitions for retrial pursuant to Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting: (1) revocation of the judgments of the first and second instances; (2) modification of the judgment to uphold the Trademark Review Board's Decision No. 38010 [2012] concerning the opposition review of Trademark No. 4312222 (graphical); and (3) costs of the first and second instances to be borne by the respondent.

After review, this Court finds that, based on the grounds of American Spider Company's petition for retrial, the focus of this Court's review is: (1) whether the Opposed Trademark and Citation Trademarks II and III constitute similar trademarks used on the same or similar goods; (2) whether Trademark No. 1212760 can serve as a basis for approving the registration of the Opposed Trademark.

Regarding the first issue: whether the Opposed Trademark and Citation Trademarks II and III constitute similar trademarks used on the same or similar goods. First, as to whether the goods categories are identical or similar. The goods designated for use under the Opposed Trademark are: clothing, baby clothing, swimwear, hats, socks, ties, scarves, belts, shoes, and gloves. The "shoes" designated under the Opposed Trademark are identical to the "shoes" approved for use under Citation Trademarks II and III; the "hats, socks, ties, scarves, gloves, and belts" designated under the Opposed Trademark are identical to the "hats, socks, ties, scarves, gloves, and belts" approved for use under Citation Trademark III; the "clothing, baby clothing, and swimwear" designated under the Opposed Trademark are closely related in function and purpose to the "hats, socks, ties, scarves, gloves, and belts" approved for use under Citation Trademark III, and thus constitute similar goods. Therefore, the goods designated under the Opposed Trademark and the goods approved for use under Citation Trademarks II and III constitute identical or similar goods. Second, as to whether the trademark signs are similar. The sign of the Opposed Trademark is a purely graphical trademark with no other constituent elements, presenting overall as a spider graphic that has undergone certain artistic treatment. The signs of Citation Trademarks II and III are also purely graphical trademarks with no other constituent elements, also presenting overall as spider graphics that have undergone certain artistic treatment. When comparing the spider graphic of the Opposed Trademark with those of Citation Trademarks II and III, they are similar in terms of spider form, overall composition, etc. In summary, the Opposed Trademark and Citation Trademarks II and III constitute similar trademarks used on identical or similar goods, and American Spider Company's ground for retrial on this issue cannot stand.

Regarding the second issue: whether Trademark No. 1212760 can serve as a basis for approving the registration of the Opposed Trademark. American Spider Company petitions for retrial, arguing that its application for registration of the Opposed Trademark is a continuation registration of the already registered Trademark No. 1212760, and thus should be approved. This Court is of the opinion that a distinction should be made between the continuation of goodwill and the continuation of a trademark. The goodwill accumulated by a market participant in the course of business operations may be transferred and continued in certain ways across different carriers of goodwill, which include identifiers capable of distinguishing the source of goods or services, such as the market participant's business name, trademark, product packaging, and trade dress. However, the market conduct of a market participant aimed at transferring or continuing goodwill is not automatically legitimate in result merely because of its legitimate purpose; it must still comply with relevant legal provisions. Specifically in this case, if American Spider Company, for reasons such as business strategy, needs to separately register a new trademark that has a certain connection with the originally registered trademark, pursuant to Article 20, Article 21, and Article 22 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended for the second time in 2001, hereinafter referred to as the 2001 Trademark Law), whether or not it has accumulated certain goodwill based on the original registered trademark, and regardless of the connection between the goods categories designated by the new trademark and the original registered trademark or between the signs used, it must file an application for registration with the trademark administration authority, and the authority shall examine it in accordance with the law. Comparing the Opposed Trademark with Trademark No. 1212760 in this case, although the goods categories designated are the same, the trademark signs are not identical. Whether the Opposed Trademark can be registered must be re-examined in accordance with the law, and it is not automatically lawful merely because of its connection with Trademark No. 1212760. Regarding trademark continuation, Article 38 of the 2001 Trademark Law provides for the renewal of registered trademarks, but no other forms of trademark continuation are provided for. Therefore, American Spider Company's ground for retrial on this issue cannot stand.

American Spider Company also petitions for retrial, arguing that the Opposed Trademark has formed a stable market pattern through continuous use and promotion. However, on this ground for retrial, American Spider Company has admitted that it has been continuously using Trademark No. 1212760. Therefore, this ground for retrial cannot stand.

In summary, the petition for retrial filed by American Spider Group Co., Ltd. does not meet the circumstances set forth in Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. This Court, pursuant to Article 74 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby rules as follows:

The petition for retrial of American Spider Group Co., Ltd. is dismissed.
